tool.name: CARP
tool.description: Comprehensive Annotation of Repeats Pipeline for plant genomes
tool.command:
## Ensure the baked-in conda tools and pipeline scripts are on PATH even ## if Galaxy execs the container with a cleaned environment. export PATH=/opt/conda/bin:/opt/pipeline/scripts:\$PATH &&
## Symlink inputs to .fasta names in the (bind-mounted) job dir so the ## pipeline and RepeatMasker see a real FASTA extension. ln -s '$genome' input_genome.fasta && #if $custom_library ln -s '$custom_library' custom_library.fasta && #end if #if $tandem_repeat_library ln -s '$tandem_repeat_library' tandem_repeat_library.fasta && #end if
mkdir -p output &&
## Build config.yaml printf '%s\n' "genome_fasta: input_genome.fasta" "output_dir: output" > config.yaml && #if $custom_library echo "custom_library: custom_library.fasta" >> config.yaml && #end if #if $tandem_repeat_library echo "tandem_repeat_library: tandem_repeat_library.fasta" >> config.yaml && #end if echo "repeatmasker_sensitivity: $advanced.repeatmasker_sensitivity" >> config.yaml && echo "repeatmasker_culling_limit: $advanced.repeatmasker_culling_limit" >> config.yaml && echo "tidecluster_reannotate_culling_limit: $advanced.tidecluster_reannotate_culling_limit" >> config.yaml && ## Maximal post-run cleanup of intermediate scratch (not exposed to the UI): ## purges the scratch FILES inside the large TideCluster tarean/kite/consensus ## trees, plus the tool workdirs. Since CARP 1.6.1 the three trees themselves ## are kept (they hold the inputs for TideCluster's per-array consensus and ## report re-render, and the kite monomer-size CSV the report reads), so an ## archived run stays re-renderable; upstream measures the file-level purge as ## still freeing 90% of their size. Manifest outputs (the served reports/GFFs) ## and their symlink targets are never deleted. echo "cleanup_intermediates: maximal" >> config.yaml &&
## Memory budget, when Galaxy knows one. CARP takes the job's allocation as ## a single -m <GB>, which sets max_memory_gb and thereby the default ## resources.mem_mb of every memory-gated rule: the make_unified_annotation ## worker pool, the three BigWig density pools, DANTE_TIR's concurrent CAP3 ## assemblies and TideCluster's TideHunter/TAREAN pools. Concurrency caps ## only; they cannot change any output. ## ## Galaxy exposes an allocation as GALAXY_MEMORY_MB, but only for some ## runners (SLURM, SGE, Kubernetes, AWS) and never for PBS/Torque or the ## local runner, so guard it like GALAXY_SLOTS. Passing it matters most in ## exactly this setting: the pipeline runs inside the container, where ## /proc/meminfo reports the whole node and the scheduler's own variables ## (PBS_RESC_MEM, SLURM_MEM_PER_NODE) have been stripped by --cleanenv, so ## CARP's auto-detection cannot see the job's limit. When the variable is ## absent we pass nothing and CARP auto-detects (scheduler environment, ## then cgroup limit, then MemAvailable). Whole GB, truncated, which errs ## low; below 1 GB pass nothing rather than -m 0, which means auto-detect. CARP_MEM_ARG='' && if [ "\${GALAXY_MEMORY_MB:-0}" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then CARP_MEM_GB=\$(( GALAXY_MEMORY_MB / 1024 )); if [ "\$CARP_MEM_GB" -gt 0 ]; then CARP_MEM_ARG="-m \$CARP_MEM_GB"; fi; fi &&
## Run the pipeline (Snakemake wrapper, threads and memory from Galaxy) /opt/pipeline/run_pipeline.py -c config.yaml -t \${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1} \$CARP_MEM_ARG &&
## Unified annotation cp output/Repeat_Annotation_Unified.gff3 '$unified_gff' &&
## Optional per-tool GFF3 outputs (none selected by default). These are ## exactly the files that also sit at the root of the results archive; ## copying them out only saves the user unpacking it. All four are ## declared in carp_manifest.json, so cleanup_intermediates: maximal ## never removes them (nor their symlink targets). #set $extra = str($extra_gff3).split(',') if $extra_gff3 else [] #if 'dante' in $extra cp output/DANTE_filtered.gff3 '$dante_gff' && #end if #if 'dante_ltr' in $extra cp output/DANTE_LTR.gff3 '$dante_ltr_gff' && #end if #if 'dante_tir' in $extra cp output/DANTE_TIR.gff3 '$dante_tir_gff' && #end if #if 'tidecluster' in $extra cp output/Tandem_repeats_TideCluster.gff3 '$tidecluster_gff' && #end if
## Main HTML report + its complete linked tree. repeat_annotation_report.html ## deep-links run_provenance.json, plotly.min.js, DANTE_LTR/, DANTE_TIR/report.html ## and TideCluster/default/ (with its report subtree), so the whole output tree ## must be served alongside it. Exclude only the bulky, non-deep-linked BigWig ## and BAM data (kept in the results archive). cp output/repeat_annotation_report.html '$report' && mkdir -p '$report.extra_files_path' && ( cd output && tar cf - --exclude='*.bw' --exclude='*.bam' --exclude='*bigwig*' . ) | ( cd '$report.extra_files_path' && tar xf - ) &&
## Complete results archive (everything). Built with python's zipfile ## via shutil, because the CARP container image ships no `zip` binary. python3 -c "import shutil; shutil.make_archive('carp_output', 'zip', 'output')" && mv carp_output.zip '$output_archive'

param.name: genome
param.label: Genome assembly (FASTA)
param.help: Plant genome assembly to annotate. Do not use on animal genomes.

param.name: custom_library
param.label: Custom repeat library (optional)
param.help: Extra RepeatMasker-format library. FASTA headers as name#class/subclass, e.g. myCopia_1#Class_I/LTR/Ty1_copia/Ale

param.name: tandem_repeat_library
param.label: Tandem repeat library (optional)
param.help: Reference tandem-repeat library used by TideCluster to name families, e.g. PisTR-B#Satellite

param.name: extra_gff3
param.label: Additional per-tool GFF3 outputs
param.help: None by default. These are the individual tool annotations that feed the unified annotation. IMPORTANT: the very same files are ALWAYS present at the root of the complete results archive, whether or not you tick a box here — ticking one only lifts that file out as a separate dataset so you do not have to unpack the archive. The unified annotation remains the authoritative, non-overlapping result.

section.name: advanced
section.title: Advanced settings: RepeatMasker speed vs. sensitivity

param.name: repeatmasker_sensitivity
param.label: RepeatMasker sensitivity
param.help: Affects ONLY the similarity-based RepeatMasker masking — the structure-based annotations (DANTE, DANTE_LTR, DANTE_TIR, TideCluster) are not affected. The default 'rush', together with culling below, makes RepeatMasker about 7.5x faster at a small sensitivity cost (roughly 1.8% fewer masked bp). This is the recommended default and is especially suitable for large genomes, where RepeatMasker dominates run time. Choose 'default' or 'quick' for maximum sensitivity when run time is not a concern.

param.name: repeatmasker_culling_limit
param.label: RepeatMasker culling limit (main search)
param.help: rmblastn -culling_limit for the main RepeatMasker step. The default 2 (culling ON) is about 3x faster at only ~0.7% fewer masked bp, by collapsing redundant per-locus hits from the de-novo library; set 0 to turn culling off for maximum sensitivity. Affects only RepeatMasker masking, not the structure-based annotations.

param.name: tidecluster_reannotate_culling_limit
param.label: RepeatMasker culling limit (TideCluster reannotation search)
param.help: Same culling for TideCluster's internal RepeatMasker, independent of the main search. The default 2 is about 3.7x faster at ~0.8% fewer masked bp; set 0 to turn it off.

data.name: dante_gff
data.label: CARP on ${genome.hid}: DANTE filtered protein domains (GFF3)

data.name: dante_ltr_gff
data.label: CARP on ${genome.hid}: DANTE_LTR complete LTR retrotransposons (GFF3)

data.name: dante_tir_gff
data.label: CARP on ${genome.hid}: DANTE_TIR TIR DNA transposons (GFF3)

tool.help:
**What it does**
The Comprehensive Annotation of Repeats Pipeline (CARP) identifies and classifies the repetitive elements of a **plant** genome assembly and merges them into a single, non-overlapping annotation. It integrates:
- **DANTE / DANTE_LTR** — intact LTR retrotransposons - **DANTE_TIR** — TIR DNA transposons - **DANTE_LINE** — LINE elements (experimental) - **TideCluster** — tandem repeats / satellites and rDNA arrays - **RepeatMasker** — genome-wide similarity masking with a CARP-built library
.. class:: warningmark
CARP was developed for plant genomes. Do not use it on animal genomes.
**Inputs**
- *Genome assembly (FASTA)* — the assembly to annotate (required). - *Custom repeat library* — optional extra RepeatMasker-format library (headers ``name#class/subclass``). - *Tandem repeat library* — optional reference library for naming tandem families in TideCluster.
**Additional per-tool GFF3 outputs**
The four checkboxes lift the individual tool annotations out as separate datasets. They are off by default and they change nothing about the run:
- ``DANTE_filtered.gff3`` — filtered DANTE protein-domain annotations - ``DANTE_LTR.gff3`` — complete LTR retrotransposons - ``DANTE_TIR.gff3`` — TIR DNA transposons - ``Tandem_repeats_TideCluster.gff3`` — tandem repeats from TideCluster
.. class:: infomark
These very same files are **always** written to the root of the complete results archive, whether or not the boxes are ticked. The checkboxes only save you unpacking the archive to get at them. For most purposes use the unified annotation instead: it is the authoritative, non-overlapping merge of all of them.
**Advanced settings: RepeatMasker speed vs. sensitivity**
These knobs affect only the similarity-based RepeatMasker masking — the structure-based annotations (DANTE, DANTE_LTR, DANTE_TIR, TideCluster) are **not** affected. The defaults (``rush`` sensitivity with culling limit 2 in both searches) are the recommended, much faster choice, especially suitable for large genomes where RepeatMasker dominates run time; the sensitivity cost is small:
- *Sensitivity* — the default ``rush`` together with culling is about **7.5x faster** than ``default`` at only ~1.8 % fewer masked bp. Use ``default`` or ``quick`` for maximum sensitivity when run time is not a concern. - *Culling limit (main search)* — default ``2`` (on) is about **3x faster** at ~0.7 % fewer masked bp; ``0`` turns culling off. - *Culling limit (TideCluster reannotation search)* — default ``2`` is about **3.7x faster** at ~0.8 % fewer masked bp; ``0`` turns it off.
**Outputs**
- *Complete results archive* (zip) — the full ``output/`` directory, including per-class GFF3 files, density BigWig tracks, summary statistics and plots. - *Unified repeat annotation* (GFF3) — ``Repeat_Annotation_Unified.gff3``, the authoritative non-overlapping annotation. - *Repeat annotation report* (HTML) — the main ``repeat_annotation_report.html`` with its complete linked tree: the DANTE_LTR, DANTE_TIR and TideCluster sub-reports and the run provenance are browsable from it. (The bulky BigWig and BAM tracks are not embedded in the report — get those from the archive.) - *Per-tool GFF3 files* (optional, off by default) — copies of ``DANTE_filtered.gff3``, ``DANTE_LTR.gff3``, ``DANTE_TIR.gff3`` and ``Tandem_repeats_TideCluster.gff3``, which are in the archive regardless.
**Version note**
CARP releases 1.0.0 to 1.3.0 built a RepeatMasker library containing no ``Class_II`` sequences, so DNA transposons were annotated only where DANTE_TIR found a complete structural element and never by similarity. This was fixed in 1.4.0; annotations produced from 1.4.0 onwards therefore differ from earlier ones (upstream measured ``Class_II`` up 25 % on an 80 Mbp genome). Re-run older analyses if DNA-transposon content matters for your assembly.
**Cluster resources**
Threads come from ``GALAXY_SLOTS``. Memory is passed on only when the job runner tells Galaxy what it allocated: if ``GALAXY_MEMORY_MB`` is defined, the wrapper converts it to whole GB and passes it as ``run_pipeline.py -m``, which sets ``max_memory_gb`` and thereby bounds every memory-gated pool in the pipeline — the unified-annotation workers, the three BigWig density pools, DANTE_TIR's concurrent CAP3 assemblies and TideCluster's TideHunter/TAREAN pools. These are concurrency caps only and cannot change any output.
Galaxy defines ``GALAXY_MEMORY_MB`` for SLURM, SGE, Kubernetes and AWS, but not for PBS/Torque or the local runner. Where it is undefined the wrapper passes nothing and CARP auto-detects, in order: the scheduler environment, then the cgroup limit, then ``MemAvailable``.
.. class:: warningmark
Auto-detection is weakest in precisely the situation Galaxy creates. The pipeline runs inside the container, where ``/proc/meminfo`` reports the whole **node** rather than the job, and Galaxy launches it with ``--cleanenv``, which strips the scheduler variables (``PBS_RESC_MEM``, ``SLURM_MEM_PER_NODE``) that CARP would otherwise read. Administrators running large genomes on a runner that does not populate ``GALAXY_MEMORY_MB`` should set it in the job destination environment; otherwise the pipeline sizes its pools against memory the job is not allowed to use, and the symptom is an OOM kill hours into the run.
**Container**
The tool runs from the CARP Singularity/Apptainer image published to GHCR (``oras://ghcr.io/kavonrtep/carp/sif:@CONTAINER_TAG@``). The Galaxy instance must have Singularity/Apptainer enabled and able to pull ``oras://`` images.
More information: https://github.com/kavonrtep/CARP
